title: Production Database Recovery Safety + Disposable Rehearsal

root_cause.forensic_limit: PostgreSQL statement logging was disabled, so the exact DROP statements are not durably recorded.

production_recovery_plan.preferred_strategy: validated replacement database plus atomic name cutover; never overwrite the damaged forensic database
steps: Confirm all PostgreSQL writers are disabled and no writer/Alembic sessions or locks exist.
Take a fresh forensic custom-format dump of current football and preserve/export football-agent_pgdata before any cutover.
Create an unmistakably named staging database and restore the SHA-verified Aug-30 candidate.
Run the rehearsed repository Alembic 0020 to 0021 upgrade against staging only.
Require exact schema hash, row counts, sequence inventory, zero canonical duplicates, zero FK orphans, clean alembic check and application read-only compatibility.
Apply no delta reconstruction unless separately approved after row-level evidence review.
Terminate application connections, rename football to a timestamped damaged/forensic database, then rename the validated staging database to football.
Re-run identity, revision, schema, data-integrity and application initialization checks before allowing any writer to resume.
Rollback by reversing database names if validation fails; retain all dumps and the original volume.
production_recovery_plan.estimated_cutover_downtime: approximately 5-15 minutes after staging validation; excludes optional delta reconstruction
conditions_before_execution: Merge/deploy the test-safety fix before any integration testing is re-enabled.
Explicitly accept the minimum known 95 fixture / 7 prediction / 1 bookmaker gap or separately approve evidence-based reconstruction.
Reconfirm an administrator-level writer freeze and take fresh forensic backup/volume preservation.
Do not include Alembic 0022 in recovery.
